subject: Product approval needed: overload error taxonomy + docs wording (Hosted API + OpenAI-compat)
body:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 18, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Product approval needed: overload error taxonomy + docs wording (Hosted API + OpenAI-compat)

Rafael,

We’re at the point where we need product sign-off on the customer-facing error taxonomy for overload protection before we lock docs + SDK behavior.

Can you share the final proposed mapping (HTTP status + Redwood error codes + Retry-After guidance), and I’ll confirm:
- what we commit to as “stable” for backward compatibility
- how we describe this in docs (esp. avoiding confusion w/ quotas/rate limits)
- any Dedicated differences we should call out explicitly

Sean / Lauren looped for exec + Dedicated alignment.

If we can align today, we can keep the docs PR on track for this week’s canary.

Nikhil
Product, Hosted API


---

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 18, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Product approval needed: overload error taxonomy + docs wording (Hosted API + OpenAI-compat)

Yep. Attaching the latest v3 summary we’ve been iterating on (pulled from ADR-0147 draft + the support sheet).

Attachment: Overload-Error-Taxonomy-v3.pdf

Key decisions we need from Product:

1) When do we return 429 vs 503?
- 429 for “admission control / client should retry” situations (capacity-based shed at edge or routing)
- 503 for “service temporarily unavailable” (regional brownout, dependency degraded, breaker open due to platform protection)

2) What is stable / contract?
- We want to commit to:
  a) status code is accurate and consistent (no more 500/502/503 mix)
  b) Retry-After header will be present for overload-shed responses (429/503)
  c) Redwood error code string (e.g., OVERLOAD_SHED_EDGE) will not change once GA
  d) OpenAI-compat will include the code in error.type and a copy in error.code

3) Backward compat concern:
Some customers currently treat 5xx as “retry forever” and 429 as “stop / rate limited”. That’s why we’re proposing clear docs: 429 here is not a quota limit; it’s overload protection and you should retry with backoff.

Proposed Redwood error codes (subset):
- OVERLOAD_SHED_EDGE (gateway admission)
- OVERLOAD_SHED_ROUTING (routing refuses based on breaker/capacity)
- OVERLOAD_SHED_RUNTIME_QUEUE_FULL
- OVERLOAD_SHED_RUNTIME_MEMORY_PRESSURE
- OVERLOAD_BREAKER_OPEN (explicit breaker open)

Also: we’re proposing that shed responses do NOT count as billable usage.

Rafael
SRE Manager


---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 18, 2025 at 10:21 AM PT
Subject: Re: Product approval needed: overload error taxonomy + docs wording (Hosted API + OpenAI-compat)

Jumping in on Dedicated alignment.

For Dedicated, customers expect “predictable capacity” and will be sensitive to 429 showing up because they interpret it as plan enforcement. I’m okay with the same payload shape + Redwood codes, but I’d prefer we bias to 503 for Dedicated pool exhaustion vs 429 unless we have a strong reason.

If we do use 429 on Dedicated, docs need a very clear callout: “not a quota limit” + Retry-After guidance + how to size capacity.

Lauren
PM, Dedicated


---

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 18, 2025 at 11:07 AM PT
Subject: Re: Product approval needed: overload error taxonomy + docs wording (Hosted API + OpenAI-compat)

Agree w/ Lauren’s concern. For Hosted API, 429 is normal/expected and aligns with “backoff and retry.” For Dedicated, 429 risks getting interpreted as “you hit a limit we imposed” rather than “your pool is temporarily saturated.”

Proposal from Product side:
- Hosted:
  - 429 for overload shedding (edge/routing/runtime)
  - 503 for regional brownout / breaker open due to platform safety (or major dependency impact)
- Dedicated:
  - default 503 for pool exhaustion / breaker open
  - 429 only for very explicit admission control scenarios where Retry-After is meaningful and short (seconds)

Docs wording needs to disambiguate:
- “Rate limits / quotas” (customer config / plan) vs
- “Overload protection” (platform protection, temporary, safe retry)

Rafael: can you confirm if the implementation can do the Dedicated bias without creating two entirely different semantics?

Nikhil


---

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 18, 2025 at 11:44 AM PT
Subject: Re: Product approval needed: overload error taxonomy + docs wording (Hosted API + OpenAI-compat)

Yes, we can do that via policy/config at the edge (status mapping by deployment mode) while keeping:
- same Redwood error code
- same response schema
- same Retry-After behavior

So e.g. OVERLOAD_SHED_ROUTING could map to:
- Hosted: 429
- Dedicated: 503

That’s clean from an SRE perspective as long as docs/SDK guidance doesn’t assume 429 only.

One nuance: OpenAI-compat clients sometimes branch hard on 429 vs 5xx.
- If we change a customer from “sometimes 500/503/timeouts” to “consistently 429 w/ Retry-After”, most clients improve.
- But a small set might stop retrying on 429. That’s why we want the docs to say explicitly: treat 429 w/ Redwood OVERLOAD_* codes as retryable.

If Product is OK, we’ll treat the following as “contracted stable” once GA:
- HTTP status per deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated) will remain consistent for each Redwood overload code
- Redwood overload code strings (OVERLOAD_*) won’t change
- Retry-After header will exist for all overload responses (and be parseable integer seconds)

Rafael


---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 18, 2025 at 12:26 PM PT
Subject: Re: Product approval needed: overload error taxonomy + docs wording (Hosted API + OpenAI-compat)

I’m supportive of the approach with two guardrails:

1) Backward compatibility statement must be explicit.
We can change status codes, but we need to guarantee:
- error body shape is stable
- clients have a deterministic way to tell overload vs “we are broken”
- Retry-After guidance is consistent

2) We should avoid creating a situation where “load shedding” pages the oncall as an incident.
If we’re returning intentional 429/503 for overload, it should be accounted separately from internal 5xx in our reporting and paging logic.

Nikhil: please ensure docs language doesn’t read like “we are down.”
Rafael: ensure support has a one-pager explaining the difference + recommended retry patterns.

Sean
Director, SRE


---

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 18, 2025 at 1:18 PM PT
Subject: Re: Product approval needed: overload error taxonomy + docs wording (Hosted API + OpenAI-compat)

Makes sense. I drafted a docs wording proposal based on this (attached). Please sanity-check tone + the explicit compatibility commitments.

Attachment: Docs-wording-proposal-overload-errors.md

Key phrasing I’m proposing for the public docs:
- “During unusually high load, Redwood may intentionally reject requests to protect overall system stability.”
- “These responses are expected during overload and are safe to retry.”
- “Overload protection is distinct from rate limits and quotas.”
- “When present, the Retry-After header indicates how long to wait before retrying.”

Compatibility section:
- “We commit that overload responses include a stable Redwood error code in the response body.”
- “For OpenAI-compatible endpoints, the Redwood error code will be surfaced in the error object.”
- “Once generally available, Redwood overload error code strings will not change without a deprecation period.”

Open question for Rafael/Sean:
Do we want to commit to “Retry-After is always present” or “best effort”? My preference: always present for the overload taxonomy we’re defining (and omit it for non-overload errors).

Nikhil


---

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 18, 2025 at 2:02 PM PT
Subject: Re: Product approval needed: overload error taxonomy + docs wording (Hosted API + OpenAI-compat)

+1 to “Retry-After always present” for OVERLOAD_* errors.

We can guarantee that because:
- edge and routing both can set it deterministically
- runtime shed points can bubble up a default Retry-After (even if it’s conservative)

Only time it might be missing is if we have a bug, and that’s exactly why we should treat it as a contract and test it.

Minor tweak request to docs wording:
- Please add a short note that Retry-After is in seconds (integer)
- Please add “use exponential backoff with jitter” (support keeps seeing synchronized retries)

Rafael


---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Nov 19, 2025 at 9:37 AM PT
Subject: Re: Product approval needed: overload error taxonomy + docs wording (Hosted API + OpenAI-compat)

Reviewed the draft doc language. Looks good with one Dedicated-specific addition:

In the Dedicated section, can we include a sentence like:
“Dedicated deployments are sized for expected peak throughput; if demand exceeds provisioned capacity, the service may return temporary overload errors (typically 503) with Retry-After.”

This helps set expectations without sounding like an SLA loophole.

Lauren


---

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Nov 19, 2025 at 4:41 PM PT
Subject: Re: Product approval needed: overload error taxonomy + docs wording (Hosted API + OpenAI-compat)

Aligned. Final decisions (Product sign-off):

1) Taxonomy contract
- Redwood overload codes (OVERLOAD_*) are stable once GA; changes require deprecation period + docs update.
- Overload responses MUST include Retry-After (integer seconds) and a customer-actionable message.
- Overload-shed responses are distinct from quota/rate limit errors.

2) HTTP mapping
- Hosted: prefer 429 for overload shedding; 503 for broader unavailability / brownout modes.
- Dedicated: prefer 503 for capacity exhaustion / breaker-open scenarios; 429 only when we’re intentionally doing short-window admission control and Retry-After is meaningful.

3) Backward compatibility
- OpenAI-compatible endpoints: include Redwood overload code in error.type and also in error.code (where supported) without breaking existing error object fields.
- Docs will instruct customers to treat 429/503 with OVERLOAD_* as retryable (exponential backoff + jitter).

Rafael: please proceed with ADR-0147 finalization on that basis and ensure ENG-4823 / openai-compat PR reflect this mapping.
Lauren: I’ll incorporate the Dedicated paragraph you suggested into the docs PR.
Sean: we’ll also ensure the public doc avoids “we’re down” language and points to status page only for regional incidents (not routine overload shedding).

Nikhil
